newsitem.title: USA: Texas natural gas storage below 1995 levels.
newsitem.headline: Texas natural gas storage below 1995 levels.

text.p: The Texas Railroad Commission on Thursday said the amount of natural gas in storage in the state was below last winter's level.
It said 206 billion cubic feet of gas were in storage as of Dec. 15, down from 214 bcf at the same time last year. Texas produces about 25 percent of the natural gas in the United States.
Despite the lower storage levels, the Railroad Commission's gas services director, Ron Kitchens, said "overall the state is in fairly good shape, especially salt caverns."

Unlike reservoir storage, salt caverns enjoy quick turnaround, Kitchens said. Kitchens said there was a big draw on salt cavern storage in late November and early December, but the caverns were now filling.

Also, the commission, which regulates energy production in Texas, set January production allowables for prorated fields at 2.29 bcf per day (bcfd), compared to 2.4 bcfd actual January, 1996 production.
